plant.habit: Single erect stalk; tillers rare in grain corn, common in sweet corn.
plant.leafArrangement: Alternate, in one vertical plane, one leaf per node.
plant.leafShape: First leaf short, oval, round-tipped (about 4 to 4.5 cm); every later leaf pointed, broad lance-shaped and longer than the one before, length peaking at about 0.68 × the final leaf number.
plant.leafOrientation: A seedling's leaf plane follows the direction the kernel was planted, so early fields look random from above; between about 40 and 50 days after planting many hybrids turn leaves toward the alley (40 to 70% of the top two leaves within 30° of perpendicular to the row by 60 days in Iowa inbreds). Modern hybrids are more upright than older ones.
plant.notes: From above a seedling is two to four leaves in one plane: its longest span is about twice the longest leaf and its width only a leaf's width (our reading), not a disc.

evidence.notes: 62 cm at rank 9 on 14-leaf plants; 88 cm at rank 16 on 26-leaf lines.

byStage.notes: 24 to 37 cm² from 2.29% cover in Shanxi; 70 to 230 cm² for 3 to 5 leaf plants in France (806 to 2,253 px at 0.25 to 0.35 cm).
Neighbours whose leaf planes lie along the row begin to touch at 14 to 20 cm in-row spacing (our estimate); counting accuracy falls from overlap (snippet).
About 520 cm² per plant from 32.2% cover at about 62,000 live plants/ha (our arithmetic); 'severe leaf overlapping'.

evidence.notes: Coarsest published counting GSD is 1.5 cm (Ohio, R² 0.94); nothing published counts corn at 3 to 5 cm.
Millimetre features: even at 0.33 cm 'weeds that resembled maize in shape and color were detected as maize'.

variation.name: Upright versus flat leaf angle
variation.effect: Upright hybrids show less projected area per plant at the same stage and keep the alley visible longer; the leaf-angle difference between upright and flat parents is 20 to 30°. Not quantified for imagery.

variation.name: Sweet corn
variation.effect: Shorter, thinner leaves and tillers that widen the plant at the base.

variation.name: Uneven emergence and replant
variation.effect: A one-week emergence gap is about two leaf stages: two plant sizes along the row. The field is staged by the 50% rule; the imagery should report both sizes.

variation.name: Stress
variation.effect: Drought leaf rolling reduces projected area and exposes soil (midday flights under-read cover); floppy shallow-planted seedlings lean the whorl off the row line.

gaps: No US table of leaf length and width by leaf rank for leaves 1 to 8 (Dwyer and Stewart 1986 not retrieved).
No measured canopy width across the row or projected area in cm² by V stage from a US source; the areas are back-calculated.
Popcorn morphology and leafy-hybrid leaf dimensions not found.
